1.

MFA No.8691/2018 has been filed by the Insurance Company and MFA No.6532/2022 has been filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') being aggrieved by the judgment dated 05.07.2018 passed by MACT, Bengaluru in MVC No.5742/2017.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 09.05.2017 at about 08.30 p.m., the claimant was walking on the side of road, on Mallimakanapura Village, Hosakote Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-50-R-575 came in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed to the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.

sentences.text: The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.

It was pleaded that he spent NC: 2023:KHC:33038 huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges,
etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. On service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and respondent No.1 only filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
It was pleaded that the petition itself is false and frivolous in the eye of law.
The age, avocation and income of the claimant and the medical expenses are denied.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant herself was examined as PW-1 and Dr.Balakrishna was examined as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.

On behalf NC:
2023:KHC:33038 of the respondents, neither examined any witness nor exhibited any document.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.3,98,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeals have been filed by the claimant as well as the Insurance Company.

6. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, at the time of the accident, the claimant was aged about 32 years.
She is a home maker and also doing tailoring work and was earning Rs.15,000/- but the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the claimant as Rs.9,000/- is on the lower side.
Secondly, due the accident, she has suffered spinal injury.
She has examined a doctor as PW-2.
In his evidence, he has deposed that the claimant has suffered spinal injury and has assessed the disability at 30%.

But the Tribunal without giving any reason, has reduced the disability to 10%
which is on the lower side.
c) Lastly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
She was treated as inpatient for a period of 6 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, she was not in a position to discharge her regular work.
She has suffered lot of pain during treatment.

Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings'
and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised following counter contentions:

4 NC: 2023:KHC:33038 a) Firstly, even though the claimant claims that she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, she has not produced any documents to establish her income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the claimant notionally.

b) Secondly, even though the doctor has assessed the whole body disability as 30% in relation to the whole spine, in a cross-examination, the doctor has clearly admitted that the claimant does not require any future surgery.
Even PW-2 is not a treated doctor and he has not produced any document to establish his statement made in the evidence.
Considering the same, the whole body disability assessed by the Tribunal 10% is on higher side.
c) Thirdly, as per the evidence of the doctor, he has clearly admitted that the claimant does not require any future surgery.

But the compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'future medical expenses' is contrary to the material available on record.

d) Fourthly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the age and avocation of the NC: 2023:KHC:33038 claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are on higher side.

e) Lastly, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 09.05.2017 due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.
The claimant claims that she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
She has not produced any documents to prove her income.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2017, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.11,000/- p.m.

5 11.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained lacerated wound over occipital region, 2X1 tenderness over lombo sacreal injine ant etc.

The doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered spinal injury and there was bulging at C-2, C-3, C-3-C-4, C-4, C- 5, C-6 of S3 vertebrae and he has assessed the disability of 30% in relation to the whole spine.
But the Tribunal has not given any reason in respect of reduction of disability to 10%.

Therefore, taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor and injuries sustained by the claimant, I am of the opinion that the whole body disability is assessed at - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:33038 20%.
The claimant is aged about 32 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,22,400/- (Rs.11,000*12*16*20%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
12.
The nature of injuries suggests that the claimant must have been under rest and treatment for a period of 03 months.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.33,000/-
(Rs.11,000*3 months) under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
13. The claimant was treated as inpatient for more than 6 days in the hospital and thereafter, has received further treatment.

Hence, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded under the head of 'food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:33038 14.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment and he has to suffer with the disability stated by the doctor throughout his life.

Considering the same, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
15.
The claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
Even though the doctor in his chief-examination has deposed that the claimant is required future surgery.
But in the cross-examination, he has admitted that at the time of discharge, she was stable and future surgery is not required.
The claimant has not produced any document even before this Court to show that she has undergone surgery.

Therefore, the claimant is not entitled for any compensation under the head of 'future medical expenses' and the compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'future medical expenses' is deducted.
